caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular, painted wooden plaque hanging from a looped string at the top center. The plaque displays the stylized head and upper face of a bearded figure with long hair, centrally placed, rendered in dark brown, black, and muted red tones with some lighter tan areas for the skin. A crown of thorns, depicted in black, encircles the top of the head. The figure’s hair falls in thick, dark strands around the sides of the face and onto the cheeks and chin. The eyes are large and outlined, and the mouth, nose, and beard are visible with rough brushstrokes. The edge of the plaque is framed by a red border with a black zigzag or triangular pattern inside, which is also bordered by a thinner tan outline. The painted surface has a weathered, cracked appearance, with several visible divisions and marks. Below the plaque, on the plain off-white background, there is handwritten text in pencil, including the words "NEW MEXICO SANTOS" in uppercase letters beneath the image, lists with numbers at the left and right, and the signature “MABEL D. CLAFLIN 1926” in the lower right corner.
title: Small Christo Head - Retablo
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
